# Open Table Formats

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/open-table-formats)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/open-table-formats/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/open-table-formats) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-open-table-formats/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-open-table-formats/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

How Iceberg, Delta Lake and DuckLake store a table, change it, clean it up, register it in a catalog and move it to another format, on one hourly pageviews table, with examples that run offline on a laptop.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For data engineers and analytics engineers who write SQL and Python and now have to decide how their lakehouse tables are stored, changed, cleaned up, shared and moved between formats.

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12.15
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python rough-lakehouse.py
```

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, every example runs again in the new version. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/open-table-formats/changes).

## Contribute
